about.tagline: A lightweight web UI for the OpenRocket engine
about.body: {{name}} is a fast, mobile-friendly app for designing and simulating model rockets. It runs the real OpenRocket physics engine — compiled to WASM and JavaScript — entirely in your browser, so there's nothing to install and nothing leaves your device.
about.ork: Full OpenRocket (.ork) support: open, edit, and save your designs round-trip.
about.scope: It's a streamlined interface over the same trusted simulation core, focused on the essentials: live CG / CP / stability, 2D & 3D views, and flight simulation. If you need more of its capabilities, please refer to <orLink>OpenRocket</orLink>.
about.wip: ⚠️ Work in progress (pre-1.0) — features may be incomplete, change, or break.
about.credits: Physics by OpenRocket (GPL-3.0), compiled to WASM and JavaScript with TeaVM.
about.enginePin: Engine extracted from OpenRocket commit <commitLink>{{ref}}</commitLink>, dated {{date}}.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: {{name}} runs entirely in your browser. There are no accounts, no tracking, no analytics, and no ads.
privacy.storage: Your designs, simulations, preferences, and any custom materials or motors are saved in your browser's local storage, on your device — never sent to us or anyone else. Clearing your browser data (or using New) removes them.
privacy.network: The app downloads its motor and component catalogs from a public content-delivery network, and when you pick a motor it may fetch that motor's thrust-curve data from a public motor database; both are cached locally and subject to those providers' terms. Otherwise the app makes no network calls with your data.
privacy.hosting: Whoever hosts the app may keep standard web-server access logs (such as IP address and timestamp), as any website does. The app itself collects nothing.
privacy.weather: When you press Fetch in the Weather dialog, the launch site’s coordinates and elevation and the chosen date go to Open-Meteo, which answers with the forecast. Nothing is sent otherwise. The requests do not name this app or the site serving it.

settings.railExitMinHint: Below this the fins have too little airflow to steer, so the rocket can weathercock into the wind or go unstable as it leaves the launcher.
settings.guideAwareRodClearanceHint: OpenRocket keeps the rocket guided for the launcher's full length, wherever its launch lugs or rail buttons sit. On, a lug guides until its aft end leaves the rod, while a rail needs two buttons and guides only until the second-to-last of them leaves it, so a single button gives no guided travel at all. Usually a little sooner off the launcher, and a slightly lower exit velocity. Off matches OpenRocket.
settings.deploySpeedWarnHint: Single deployment (no drogue): above this speed, opening the parachute risks zippering the airframe or tearing the canopy.
settings.mainHighSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: above this the MAIN is coming out too fast — usually a drogue too small to slow the rocket, or a main set to deploy too high.
settings.mainLowSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: below this the main opens while the rocket is barely descending, which normally means it deployed near apogee — a slow, drifty descent from full altitude.
settings.drogueLowSpeedWarnHint: Dual deployment: below this the drogue comes out too slowly at apogee to inflate properly. Applies only to a stage carrying a chute or streamer marked as a drogue.
settings.materialsNote: What a newly added part is made of. The material is written onto the part when you add it, so it shows in the panel and travels with the design. Parts already in the rocket are not changed.

nosecone.conical: A conical nose cone has a profile of a triangle.
nosecone.ogive: An ogive nose cone has a profile that is a segment of a circle. The shape parameter value 1 produces a tangent ogive, which has a smooth transition to the body tube, values less than 1 produce secant ogives.
nosecone.ellipsoid: An ellipsoidal nose cone has a profile of a half-ellipse with major axes of lengths 2×Length and Diameter.
nosecone.power: A power series nose cone has a profile of Radius × (x / Length)k where k is the shape parameter. For k=0.5 this is a ½-power or parabolic nose cone, for k=0.75 a ¾-power, and for k=1 a conical nose cone.
nosecone.parabolic: A parabolic series nose cone has a profile of a parabola. The shape parameter defines the segment of the parabola to utilize. The shape parameter 1.0 produces a full parabola which is tangent to the body tube, 0.75 produces a 3/4 parabola, 0.5 produces a 1/2 parabola and 0 produces a conical nose cone.
nosecone.haack: The Haack series nose cones are designed to minimize drag. The shape parameter 0 produces an LD-Haack or Von Karman nose cone, which minimizes drag for fixed length and diameter, while a value of 0.333 produces an LV-Haack nose cone, which minimizes drag for fixed length and volume.

transition.conical: A conical transition has straight sides.
transition.ogive: An ogive transition has a profile that is a segment of a circle. The shape parameter value 1 produces a tangent ogive, which has a smooth transition to the body tube at the aft end, values less than 1 produce secant ogives.
transition.ellipsoid: An ellipsoidal transition has a profile of a half-ellipse with major axes of lengths 2×Length and Diameter. If the transition is not clipped, then the profile is extended at the center by the corresponding radius.
transition.power: A power series transition has a profile of Radius × (x / Length)k where k is the shape parameter. For k=0.5 the transition is ½-power or parabolic, for k=0.75 a ¾-power, and for k=1 conical.
transition.parabolic: A parabolic series transition has a profile of a parabola. The shape parameter defines the segment of the parabola to utilize. The shape parameter 1.0 produces a full parabola which is tangent to the body tube at the aft end, 0.75 produces a 3/4 parabola, 0.5 produces a 1/2 parabola and 0 produces a conical transition.
transition.haack: The Haack series nose cones are designed to minimize drag. These transition shapes are their equivalents, but do not necessarily produce optimal drag for transitions. The shape parameter 0 produces an LD-Haack or Von Karman shape, while a value of 0.333 produces an LV-Haack shape.

warnHelp.RECOVERY_HIGH_SPEED: The recovery device opened while the rocket was still moving fast. The shock loads the airframe and the canopy at once: it can zipper the body tube, tear the chute or pull the shroud lines out. Deploy nearer apogee, or fly dual-deployment with a drogue and a lower main.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_MAIN_HIGH_SPEED: On a dual-deployment flight the main should open slowly, already under drogue. This one opened fast enough to risk the same zippering and canopy damage — usually a drogue that is too small to slow the rocket, or a main set to deploy too high.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_MAIN_LOW_SPEED: The main opened while the rocket was barely descending, which normally means it deployed at or close to apogee. Nothing breaks, but the point of dual deployment is lost: the rocket floats down from full altitude and drifts a long way downwind.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_DROGUE_LOW_SPEED: The drogue opened while the rocket was barely moving, so it does little to stabilize the descent. Usually a drogue deployed well before apogee.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_LAUNCH_ROD: A recovery device deployed while the rocket was still on the launcher. Check the ejection delay and the deployment settings: as simulated, the flight ends at the pad.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_LAUNCH_ROD_rail: A recovery device deployed while the rocket was still on the rail. Check the ejection delay and the deployment settings: as simulated, the flight ends at the pad.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_LAUNCH_ROD_rod: A recovery device deployed while the rocket was still on the rod. Check the ejection delay and the deployment settings: as simulated, the flight ends at the pad.
warnHelp.RECOVERY_DROGUE_NO_MAIN: A drogue deploys but no main follows, so the rocket descends the whole way on the drogue alone. That is a fast landing unless the drogue is sized to take it.
warnHelp.NO_RECOVERY_DEVICE: Nothing deploys, so the rocket falls ballistic and the landing speed below is what it hits the ground at.
warnHelp.LargeAOA: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow exit from the launcher.
warnHelp.LargeAOA.str1: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow exit from the launcher.
warnHelp.LargeAOA.str2: The rocket flew at an angle of attack outside the range the Barrowman method is valid for, so the aerodynamic numbers around that point are approximate. Common in strong wind or just after a slow exit from the launcher.
warnHelp.SUPERSONIC: Part of the flight is supersonic, where the extended Barrowman method is an approximation. Treat the drag and stability figures through that region as indicative.

windProfile.title: Wind Profile Editor
windProfile.referenceNote: A sounding is published above sea level; a range briefing is given above the ground. At a high launch site the two describe different winds.
windProfile.duplicateAltitude: Two levels share an altitude. Each level needs its own, and the simulation cannot run until one of them moves.
windProfile.csvFormat: CSV columns: altitude, speed, direction, stddev (optional), in meters, m/s and degrees. Importing replaces the profile.

csv.missingColumns: Needs altitude, speed and direction columns.
csv.badNumber: Line {{line}} has a value that is not a number.
csv.noData: No wind levels found in that file.
csv.unreadable: That file could not be read.

limits.rodAngle: Launcher angle is {{value}} from vertical, above the {{limit}} the NAR and Tripoli safety codes allow.
limits.rodAngle_rail: Launch rail angle is {{value}} from vertical, above the {{limit}} the NAR and Tripoli safety codes allow.
limits.rodAngle_rod: Launch rod angle is {{value}} from vertical, above the {{limit}} the NAR and Tripoli safety codes allow.
limits.wind: Wind speed is {{value}}, above the {{limit}} the NAR and Tripoli safety codes allow.
limits.refused: "{{name}}" was not run — its launch conditions are outside the safety codes.

panes.maximize: Expand the drawing to the whole window

print.title: 3D print export
print.intro: Every part of this design that has a printable solid. Parachutes, shock cords, mass components and rail buttons have no body to print, so they are not listed.
print.nothing: Nothing in this design has a printable solid.
print.placeOnPlate: Place each part on the build plate
print.orientationNote: Parts keep the orientation they have in the rocket — the axis runs along X, so bodies arrive lying down. Use your slicer’s lay-flat or rotate to stand them up.

placeSearch.title: Find a place
placeSearch.label: Place, postal code, coordinates or map link
placeSearch.hint: Choosing a place sets the site's latitude, longitude and elevation.
placeSearch.none: No places found. Try a nearby town, or paste the coordinates.
placeSearch.shortLink: That is a shortened link, which hides the place behind a redirect. Open it, then paste the full address from the browser, or the coordinates.
placeSearch.elevationUnknown: elevation not found; the site's elevation stays as it is

location.label: Saved location
location.deleteConfirm: Delete the saved location “{{name}}”? This cannot be undone.
location.saveFailed: That location could not be saved — your browser storage may be full or blocked.
location.apply: Use this location for the current simulation
location.empty: No saved locations yet. Save one from the Launch site card on the Simulations tab, so you do not have to retype a field’s coordinates.
location.name: Name
location.duplicateName: Another location already has this name.
location.needsSite: Enter a latitude and longitude first — a launch location is a place, and half of one would save as 0°, 0°.
location.pickHint: Select a location on the left to edit it, or add a new one.
location.discardConfirm: Discard the changes to this location?
location.applyNeedsSave: Save or discard your changes before using this location.

map.label: Launch site map
map.title: Launch site
map.pick: Click the map to move the location.
map.keysPick: Arrow keys move the map, plus and minus zoom, and Enter puts the location at the center.
map.keysView: Arrow keys move the map, and plus and minus zoom.
map.noCoords: Enter a latitude and longitude to place the location.

sweep.title: Drift sweep
sweep.experimentalNote: A planning aid, not a range clearance: the region has not been checked against a real recovery.
sweep.stale: The design has changed since this sweep was flown.
sweep.noLandings: The wind sweep produced no landings.

weather.title: Weather from Open-Meteo
weather.needSite: Set the launch site’s latitude and longitude first.
weather.noHour: The answer has no data for that hour.
weather.archiveNoAloft: For a date this far back only surface conditions are available, with no winds or atmosphere aloft.
weather.useTerrain: Use the terrain elevation, {{terrain}}, for the site (now {{site}})
weather.forecastNote: A forecast is a model’s estimate, not a measurement.

dateRefusal.tooFarAhead: Open-Meteo forecasts up to 15 days ahead.

error.offline: Could not reach Open-Meteo. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.timeout: Open-Meteo did not answer in time. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.aborted: Canceled. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.refused: Open-Meteo refused the request: {{detail}}. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.badKey: Open-Meteo did not accept the API key in Settings, Launch. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.quota: Open-Meteo’s free limit is used up for now. Try again later, or add an API key in Settings, Launch. Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.http: Open-Meteo answered with an error ({{detail}}). Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.shape: Open-Meteo’s answer could not be read ({{detail}}). Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.units: Open-Meteo answered in units the app does not read ({{detail}}). Your launch conditions are unchanged.
error.noData: Open-Meteo has no data for that date here. Your launch conditions are unchanged.

weather.keyNote: Optional. Without a key, weather comes from Open-Meteo’s free service, which is for non-commercial use. A key from a paid Open-Meteo plan removes its limits. The key is kept only in this browser.
weather.keyNotSaved: The key could not be saved in this browser.

source.otherSite: The launch site has moved since it was fetched.
source.old: Fetched over 3 hours ago. A newer forecast may differ.

weather.reused: Reused from {{time}}. Open-Meteo is asked again after 30 minutes.

env.note: The air as the flight met it, recorded on the way up and back down, from the ground to apogee at {{apogee}}.
env.noData: This result has no atmosphere data. Run the simulation again.

landing.title: Landing
landing.flyHours: Fly the hours around this forecast
landing.flyHoursNote: Flies this design under the forecast for each hour from two before to two after, as the forecast stands now.
landing.noForecast: Fill the launch conditions with Get weather… to see how the landing moves over the hours around the forecast.
landing.failed: The flights could not be completed.

landing.title: Landing estimator
landing.intro: Where a rocket comes down, from a site, a forecast hour, its apogee and its descent rates. This is an estimate: the flight up is not modeled and the rates are the ones you type. A rocket designed here gets its landing from the simulation, on the Results tab.
landing.siteElevationHint: Leave blank to use the terrain model's height at the site.
landing.mainAltitude: Main opens above the pad at
landing.mainAboveApogee: The main has to open below apogee.
landing.empty: Set the site, the hour and the flight, then press Estimate landing.
landing.estimateNote: An estimate from typed descent rates. The zone covers {{descents}} descents: {{hours}} forecast hours, wind speed 20% either way, direction 15° either way, and descent rate 10% either way.
landing.flatGround: The ground's shape could not be fetched, so the landing is on flat ground at the pad's height.
landing.surfaceWindOnly: Open-Meteo's record for this date has only the wind near the ground, so the whole descent drifts on it.
landing.mapLabel: Landing estimate seen from above, landing {{distance}} from the pad

chuteTool.title: Parachute sizing
chuteTool.intro: The canopy that lands a rocket at a chosen descent rate, from what comes down, the canopy's drag coefficient and the air at the site. An estimate from the descent equation. A parachute on a designed rocket shows the same figures under Descent sizing in its editor.
chuteTool.massHint: What comes down under the canopy: the rocket after its propellant has burned.
chuteTool.empty: Enter the descent mass and the canopy's Cd.

rail.title: Off the rail
rail.intro: How a rocket leaves the rail on a given motor: its thrust to weight, the speed it leaves the rail at, and how far a crosswind turns it. A designed rocket gets these from its simulation, on the rail departure event.
rail.dryMassHint: The motor's loaded mass comes from the catalog and is added to this.
rail.forecastWindGust: Forecast wind {{wind}} at 10 m, gusting to {{gust}}, {{when}}.
rail.empty: Choose a motor, and enter the rocket's mass and the rail length.
rail.noLiftoff: The motor's thrust never exceeds the rocket's weight, so it does not leave the pad.
rail.stalls: The rocket slows to a stop before it reaches the end of the rail.
rail.twrAtExit: Thrust to weight, leaving the rail
rail.rules: Amber marks an average thrust to weight under {{ratio}} : 1, a rail exit under {{speed}} (the minimum in Settings), or a weathercock angle over {{angle}}°. The heaviest rocket meets the first two.
rail.estimateNote: An estimate: no drag, no rail friction, and the rail taken as vertical, so the real exit is a little slower.
